A server-rendered root page takes path parameters from its filename. A `-:name` part is a parameter and the hyphens beside it separate segments: `event-:id.html` serves /event/:id, `event-:id-rsvps.html` serves /event/:id/rsvps, `org-:org-team-:id.html` serves /org/:org/team/:id; `my-events-:id.html` serves /my-events/:id.

The segment binds like a query-string value, with the same escaping: `:id` or `:param_id` in gotmpl `queries:`, `{{.param_id}}` in the gotmpl body, `{{param_id}}` in mustache and in `<query sql="... WHERE id = {{param_id}}">` (bound as `?`). The path value wins over a `?id=` of the same name. A record that does not exist renders the page's empty state (a `LIMIT 1` query gives an empty map), so answer "not found" in the template. /event and /event/ are not this page (404 unless another page or file serves them).

Rules: the name is letters, digits and _ (not starting with a digit), each name once, and the filename starts with a fixed part (`:id.html` would answer every top-level path). Push and `benmore check` refuse other uses of `:` in a root page filename, and a parameter page whose route another page, a flow or a framework route already answers (two pages `event-:id.html` and `event-:slug.html` are one route).

Discovery: sitemap.xml, llms.txt, feed.xml and the PWA precache leave parameter pages out (a route pattern has no record to crawl). Put the record URLs in your own `static/sitemap.xml` when crawlers should find them.

SEO head: with `seo.url` set, a parameter page's `<link rel="canonical">`, `og:url` and the WebPage/BreadcrumbList JSON-LD name the requested record (`https://site/event/42`, each value re-escaped as one segment, never the query string). Every other page keeps its route as canonical, so query-parameter detail pages (`/event?id=1`, `/event?id=2`) still share the canonical `/event`: give records their own URL with a path parameter. Without `seo.url` no canonical link is emitted.

Title: `title:` (or `<page title=...>`) is fixed text and every record of a parameter page shows it; it cannot read the record or a parameter. A page with no title is named from its fixed segments (/event/:id → `Event`, /event/:id/rsvps → `Event Rsvps`). Put the record's name in the page body (an `<h1>`).
